Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Segregated tenancy pilot ask + initial sizing data

Maria / Procure team —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our conversation, I put together a concise pilot proposal to validate MedSys' PHI isolation and latency requirements before moving to committed capacity. Key constraints you called out: latency p95 <= 120ms for synchronous chart-lookup calls, bursty peaks up to 1.2k QPS for short windows, and strict audit logging retained for 7 years.

Chief ask for procurement: confirm whether MedSys will sign a 3-month pilot that allows burst (shared infra) for the first 30 days and then move to a segregated dedicated cluster if the SLA checks pass. The pilot we propose:
- Dedicated reserved pool toggle: start with 6xA40-equivalent GPUs (or A10X equivalent on your preferred cloud SKU) configured as a private, isolated tenancy (VPC peering).
- Burst overlay: allow an extra 3 GPU worth of burst capacity from a reserved buffer for traffic spikes during the pilot.
- KV/prefix caching enabled for chart-lookup flows to reduce token re-run costs.
- Observability: token-level traces and audit logs forwarded to your KMS-backed storage (we will provide SOC2 attestation).

I attached a lightweight CAPEX vs OPEX sheet and an architecture sketch for the segregated tenancy approach. Laura / Monica — please note the timeline constraint: MedSys needs a procurement decision by end of month to meet their Q2 pilot window.

Next steps: Maria, can you confirm procurement cadence and whether your security team needs any additional artifacts to greenlight the VPC-based pilot?

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Michael —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
1) PHI requirement: medsys will need the private VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS; shared tenancy is not acceptable for production but is tolerable for a pre-prod pilot if the data is tokenized and flagged.
2) Cost question: procurement wants to see the delta between running isolated dedicated vs starting in a burst-to-commit pilot model. Please break down estimated monthly run-rate for both paths (pilot then commit) for the 3-month window.
3) Timeline: procurement can issue a PO within 3 weeks if the numbers look reasonable and security gets SOC2 + key management notes. We will need a single point of contact for SSO/KMS integration.

Also, Thomas from Healix is copied — they are our cloud integrator and will own the VPC setup.

Regards,
Maria Garcia

Option A — Pilot (burst-to-commit):
- Pilot (month 1): 6 reserved GPUs + 3 burst units on-demand. Estimated run-rate: $68k for month 1 (includes setup, logging retention to KMS for 7 years, and 24/7 support).
- Month 2–3 (if still pilot): baseline $52k / month (reserving 6 GPUs), burst usage billed at actual; we typically see a 20-35% delta during spikes.

Option B — Private Dedicated (commit from day 1):
- 9 GPU equivalent dedicated cluster, annualized rate pro-rated monthly: $49k / month (lower unit cost, but requires a 12-month commit for pricing above).
- Includes canary lanes, retired-fallback model variants, and audit exports.

Happy to run a scenario with your actual QPS distribution if you can share sample telemetry.

Maria + team —

I put together a compact capacity matrix and a tiling plan based on the numbers you provided in the deck. High level:
- Baseline synchronous QPS: 200 sustained; spikes up to 1.2k for 10–20 minute windows during shift changes.
- Workload profile: short-prompt, chart-lookup patterns with average prompt length ~120 tokens and KV cache hit expected ~55% for repeated charts.

Sizing suggestion (pilot -> commit):
- Pilot month 1 (burst-to-commit): 6 x A40-equivalent dedicated nodes (handles steady-state + most spikes via caching) + 3 burst nodes registered to a pre-approved buffer. Cache warm-up script included in onboarding.
- Transition trigger: on two-week rolling p95 < 110ms and spike success rate > 99.5%.
- Commit target: 8 nodes for production minimum (for expected QPS headroom and rolling upgrades); with quantized model path enabled we recommend q4_8bit variants for the less sensitive models to save ~20% GPU memory and lower cost.

Procurement artifacts you'll need from us: PO-ready line items, SOC2 report, KMS integration checklist, and network diagram (attached). I also noted the estimated change in monthly burn per option and put them in the CAPEX/OPEX workbook.

Questions for procurement: will MedSys accept a month-to-month beginning pilot that converts to a 12-month commitment automatically unless cancelled with 30 days notice? That simplifies billing for both sides.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

2) Redwood will provide a one-time pilot credit that covers up to $15k of first-month burst overages.
3) Deliverables before start: signed MAP, PO for pilot month, SSO + KMS runbook, SOC2 report, and network diagram.
4) Integration owner: Thomas Liu (Healix) to coordinate VPC peering; Laura will lead technical onboarding from Redwood side.
